title: Close words. Long way round.
question: Do pages that sound alike sit close in the hyperlink network?

method.representation: Lexical similarity, not dense embeddings: reuse Week 6 globally title-masked TF-IDF, raw term frequency times ln(N/df), L2 normalization and cosine. No stopword list, stemming or smoothing.
method.tokenization: Week 5 Unicode letter tokens, case-folded with normalized apostrophes; remove terminal possessive 's, split at hyphens, exclude numerals.
method.mask: Reuse the Week 6 global title mask from canonical Wikipedia IDs: URL-decode, replace underscores, remove parenthetical qualifiers, tokenize, retain words of at least two letters except and/of/the/for/in, then remove every occurrence from every document. Names, aliases and team labels absent from these title tokens can remain.
method.distance: Unweighted shortest path after ignoring hyperlink direction, using only the frozen 303-node roster. A missing path stays null/disconnected and is never treated as distance 4+ or infinity. Sorted-neighbor breadth-first search chooses a reproducible shortest route when several exist.
method.comparison: Each article chooses its highest-cosine alternative among all other roster pages, including unreachable pages. Count these directed choices once per source; reciprocal choices count twice. Baseline is all ordered source-target choices: every source has the same N-1 alternatives and the same weight. This is a complete finite census and descriptive comparison, not a randomized experiment or semantic accuracy test.
method.ranking: Compute and rank every unordered pair by full-precision cosine descending, then canonical source/target ID ascending for ties. The displayed three cases are exactly ranks 1-3 after filtering to finite distance >=4; that threshold is an exploratory display choice, not a fitted boundary. Disconnected pairs are ranked and inspected separately.
method.case_selection: Read the three highest-cosine unordered pairs with a finite shortest path of at least four links, plus the highest-cosine disconnected pair. These are deliberately selected exceptions, not a random sample or an estimate of semantic accuracy.
method.terms: For each shared retained term, contribution is the product of its two L2-normalized TF-IDF weights; shares divide this contribution by total cosine. The ten largest contributions are exported.
method.evidence: Explorer passages are exact frozen-text windows around the FIRST occurrence of the largest contributing term, not a relevance score. Curated cases use literal inspected excerpts. All offsets are half-open Python character offsets into decoded UTF-8-sig archive text, not byte offsets. before/after preserve additional context.
method.rounding: Rank and choose before rounding. Export similarities, contributions and shares to nine decimal places. All-source nearest choices include zero cosines if required; zero vectors have cosine zero.
